1. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the Vigilance department.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 482 BNSS, filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 13(2) & 13(1)(a) of P.C.Act.
4.
It is stated by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is a Government employee.
Further, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has been entangled falsely in a case of misappropriation.
He further contended that since the Petitioner is a Government employee there is no chance of his absconding.

He also contended that the Petitioner is ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation before the I.O.
5.

Petitioner is required for the purpose of investigation.

6. Considering such submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and on careful examination of the materials on record, the Petitioner is directed to surrender and move for bail before the leaned Special Jude, Vigilance,Phulbani in G.R.Case No.03 of 2024 (V) rising out of Berhampur Vigilance P.S.Case No.07 of 2024 within three weeks from today.

In such eventuality,
learned court in seisin over the matter shall do well to release the Petitioner on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case, but subject to the following conditions:
i) shall cooperate with the investigation and appear before the I.O. as and when required for the purpose of investigation and shall produce all the relevant documents in his possession before the I.O.
ii) shall not tamper with the evidence of the prosecution witnesses iii) shall appear before the trial court if not prevented by sufficient cause.
7. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
8. Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
( ADITYA KUMAR MOHAPATRA) JUDGE RKS Location: High Court of Orissa Subrat Mallick vs State Of Odisha .....
